events.description: US-Israel war with Iran began; six weeks of hot war until the ceasefire; the Strait of Hormuz became an issue only after this date.
Two-week US-Iran ceasefire agreed 'last week' in exchange for Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad failed; US 15-point plan vs Iranian 10-point plan had nothing in common.
Iran said it may have misplaced mines in the Omani part of the waterway, making the Strait unsafe.
US 'blockade' of shipping using Iranian ports through the Strait of Hormuz took effect ('yesterday'/'today'); Iran announced a counter-blockade.
Russia, China and France defeated a UN Security Council resolution to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Trump promised the Iranian people he was coming to their rescue and they would take control of their country.
Iran attacked Qatar, Oman and Gulf infrastructure (desalination, power plants) as well as US bases.
Houthis made token missile/drone attacks on Israel that were intercepted; neither Israel nor the US retaliated.
Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban in a 'hot border war' over Taliban support for the TTP.
Pakistan 'only just fought a war with India'.
Pakistani Defence Minister in hot water for posting threats against Israel.
Zelensky visited the Arabian Peninsula marketing Ukrainian air-defense help against Iranian attacks.
Roggio witnessed tons of potassium cyanide dug up at a missile base in Mosul.
Roggio and Fitton-Brown began discussing the UN Monitoring Team reports together.

key_claims: The US and Israel are winning the conventional war against Iran, but Iran holds the advantage in the unconventional war via the mined/closed Strait of Hormuz and by outlasting Washington.
Trump's 'blockade' should be framed as breaking Iran's illegal blockade and shutting Iranian ports; stopping 90% of Iran's oil exports could collapse its economy within weeks.
US communication of war aims has been catastrophic; the five files are nuclear, missiles, proxies, human rights/regime change and (since 28 Feb) the Strait.
Pakistan hosts US-Iran talks despite a hot border war with the Afghan Taliban, who back the TTP's goal of an Islamic Emirate of Pakistan — the 'wheel of jihad' Pakistan built.
A jihadi nuclear-armed state in Islamabad is the strategic nightmare; Fitton-Brown wants Pakistan's democracy to survive despite Roggio's schadenfreude.
The Houthis are close Iranian allies who take their own decisions; they are keeping their powder dry on Bab el-Mandeb pending a US-Iran deal or renewed war.
The war is pushing GCC states together, exposing Qatari and Omani 'footsie' with Iran, and showing Ukraine as an ally against the Iran-Russia axis.
Iran's pounding is a lesson to Sharaa's Syria that permanent conflict with Israel and the US ends in disaster.
